summary: Onboarding is making steady progress. Key remaining blockers are VPC peering details, KMS key access for Redwood Private test, and customer scheduling for a perf run. Agreed to target an end-to-end perf run next week. Redwood to share updated security docs and network diagram. Customer to provide network/IAM details and sanitized sample data.
topics: Security: KMS, audit logs, SOC2 artifacts
transcript:
[00:00] Ava Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll give folks a few more seconds. Good morning Laura, Ravi, Maya.
[00:08] Laura Kim: Morning Ava, hi Diego.
[00:10] Diego Morales: Morning all. I'm going to kick off with a quick status — I have a screen but I'll just talk through.
[00:15] Ava: Agenda today — quick onboarding status, security updates, perf run planning, then open Qs.
[00:22] Ravi Desai: Sounds good. Quick status from our side — SSO is half done, our IdP team still needs the SAML metadata from Redwood. Maya is handling KMS questions.
[00:30] Maya Singh: Right, KMS is a little sticky — we need to confirm whether Redwood will bring a customer-managed key or if we hand over a key for the pilot. Also, audit log retention details.
[00:40] Diego: For the pilot we typically recommend customer-managed KMS for Private deployments, that way you retain control. We can also do a limited scoped key if you prefer. There may be a small setup on our side for key rotation.
[00:50] Laura: Ok, customer-managed KMS sounds preferable. Can you send the exact IAM policy we need?
[00:55] Ava: Yes we'll send a policy template. I'll add that to the security pack.
[01:00] Diego: On the networking front, I tried the VPC peering test last week but I only had partial info; we still need the peering CIDR and the NAT gateway details — basically the firewall egress rules for our test hosts.
[01:12] Ravi: We'll get that. Are there specific ports? Do you need TLS inspection exceptions?
[01:18] Diego: Ports are standard https 443, and for telemetry we use a secured channel — no plain text. We do need the peering to allow our IPs. I'll paste a short list after the call.
[01:28] Maya: Also, what's the plan for data residency? Some of our datasets are EU-only, others are US. This POC will run US but we'll need to confirm later.
[01:36] Ava: Noted — we'll record that as a constraint for the rollout plan.
[01:40] Diego: Regarding the actual POC tests — can you confirm the sample dataset size and typical request patterns? We need a representative prompt set to measure batching behavior, KV cache hits, and tail latency.
[01:52] Laura: We can provide a few hundred examples of anonymized notes, and a traffic shape: mostly 1-3 request/sec avg per user with bursts of 40-50 RPS during batch processing windows.
[02:04] Diego: Perfect. That will help us set batch sizes; Redwood's runtime does continuous batching and prefix caching — sometimes transcribed as 'KV cash' in older docs — which will change unit cost.
[02:15] Laura: Haha, yes we've seen that typo.
[02:17] Ava: On security docs — Diego, can you confirm which artifacts we will include in the pack? Last time you mentioned SOC2, network diagrams, SAML flow, and a KMS policy template.
[02:26] Diego: Yes I'll include SOC2 summary, the private deployment network diagram, sample IAM policy, and a short runbook for key management. I'll upload to the shared drive and post the link here.
[02:36] Maya: Please include audit log retention specifics — our compliance needs 1 year minimum.
[02:40] Diego: We'll include default retention and options.
[02:43] Ava: Quick question from Laura — did Redwood recommend Dedicated or Private for this POC?
[02:48] Laura: We originally thought Dedicated but given the compliance we might need Private.
[02:52] Diego: For POC it's flexible. Dedicated is faster to stand up since it's managed by Redwood, but Private (VPC) is closer to your security posture. For performance benchmarking, Dedicated gives more predictable throughput; Private can be tuned but needs the network plumbing.
[03:06] Ravi: Ok, we'd prefer Private to validate SSO and KMS but if the perf run needs Dedicated, can we do a temporary switch?
[03:14] Diego: Totally, we can run the perf tests on a dedicated pool and then show how Private maps to that performance with config changes.
[03:20] Laura: That sounds good.
[03:22] Ava: Let's aim to run the perf test on Dedicated on 2027-07-13 and have a follow-up to review results.
[03:28] Ravi: Works for me.
[03:30] Maya: Quick note on profiling — we want 99th percentile under 300ms for short prompts, is that realistic?
[03:37] Diego: For 1-2k token prompts maybe. It depends on the model variant and quantization. If you need lower tail latency we can pin to a smaller context model or reduce quantization. There's a tradeoff cost vs latency.
[03:48] Laura: We're also tracking cost. Any rough numbers per 1k tokens on Redwood Dedicated?
[03:53] Diego: Rough ballpark for a mid-sized model is $0.01 - $0.03 per 1k tokens depending on batching and caching. We'll provide a cost-model spreadsheet after the perf run.
[04:04] Ava: I'll share the sample cost model and the benchmark sheet.
[04:08] Ravi: On the SAML metadata — who should I send it to?
[04:11] Ava: Send to me (ava@redwood.ai) and Diego, and we'll ensure the IdP config is updated.
[04:16] Laura: Great.
[04:18] [04:18] Diego: I'll also flag an item — if you want to test private data we recommend doing a small ingestion job and end-to-end call so we can validate KV cache and prefix behavior. That will help the perf numbers feel real.
[04:30] Maya: Ok we'll prepare a small ingest, but need guidance on sanitization.
[04:34] Diego: I'll add a short doc on acceptable anonymization patterns.
[04:38] Laura: Any blockers on our side for the perf run?
[04:41] Ravi: The main blocker is the network info and the SAML metadata; KMS policy is also pending. Once those are in we can schedule internal windows.
[04:49] Ava: Good — so action items are clear. Anything else from the customer?
[04:53] Laura: One more — your roadmap mention about model fallbacks and automatic routing, can that be part of a demo? We want to see graceful degradation if a node is saturated.
[05:03] Diego: Yes we can demo smart routing and automatic fallback — it's more of a runtime feature. We can include a short demo during the results review meeting.
[05:11] Maya: Also please include log samples so our security folks can see what events are captured.
[05:15] Diego: Will do.
[05:17] Ava: Ok let's recap next steps — Redwood sends security pack + IAM/KMS templates by Friday 2027-07-09, Diego uploads perf plan and anonymization guide by 2027-07-08, customer provides network CIDR and SAML metadata by 2027-07-10, and we run perf on 2027-07-13.
[05:34] Laura: Confirmed.
[05:36] Ravi: Confirmed.
[05:37] Maya: Confirmed.
[05:38] Ava: Great — I'll send notes and calendar invites for the perf run and follow-up.
[05:43] [05:43] Laura: Thanks everyone, appreciate it.
[05:45] Ava: Thanks all, bye.

Notes / Links shared: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack (security pack, SOC2 summary), https://redwood.example.com/network-diagram (private deployment diagram), shared drive: https://drive.company/shared/nexa/poc (sample dataset upload location).
